title: Finding the Maximum: Critical Point of an Objective Function
caption_md: Consider the objective function $A(x) = -2x^2 + 8x + 3$, which models a quantity we want to maximize. Setting $A'(x) = -4x + 8 = 0$ gives the critical point $x = 2$. The tangent line at $x = 2$ is horizontal (slope $= 0$), confirming this is a critical point. Since $A''(x) = -4 < 0$, the second-derivative test tells us this is a local maximum. Notice how the endpoints of the domain $[0, 5]$ give smaller values: $A(0) = 3$ and $A(5) = -17$. On a closed interval, always compare the critical-point value with the endpoint values.
